claims.statement: 186 orders allocated overnight to east node are stuck in 'allocated, awaiting pickup' state since 06:00; carriers are not collecting them
claims.corroboration: Incident channel (tier-2, reviewed) + Observability alert (tier-1, verified, distinct owner) confirm 9% of overnight allocations held on east node only since 06:00
claims.limitation: Alert cannot attribute cause; observability gap prevents carrier confirmation visibility

claims.statement: All 186 held orders are flagged by the allocator as split-reservation exceptions
claims.corroboration: Fulfillment report (tier-2, reviewed) states every held order flagged as split-reservation exception; reports began 06:00 and continue
claims.limitation: Does not explain causality: is split-reservation intended to hold orders, or is holding a secondary defect?

claims.statement: Allocation rule set v18 went live at 22:00 last night; it changed multi-node order reservation to prioritize east node first
claims.corroboration: Change record (tier-1, verified) confirms v18 live 22:00; regression suite passed
claims.limitation: Passed regression does not guarantee production correctness on split-reservation edge cases or scaling effects

claims.statement: System observability gap: internal dashboards lack visibility into carrier's pickup confirmation state; Inventory Control cannot see carrier-side records
claims.corroboration: Observability assessment (tier-1, verified) explicitly names the gap
claims.limitation: Gap prevents discriminating allocation defect from carrier-side failures

claims.statement: No recent warehouse system changes impacting allocation or scheduling
claims.corroboration: Release w41 (tier-1, verified) lists only printer drivers and report exports

claims.statement: Allocation rule v18's east-node-first reservation logic is triggering split-reservation exceptions that incorrectly hold orders from carrier pickup
claims.corroboration: Temporal correlation: v18 deployed 22:00, stuck orders began 06:00 (8 hours later, after overnight allocation window); all affected orders on reserved node; all flagged with split-reservation exception
claims.limitation: Correlation does not prove causation; requires audit of split-reservation logic and its interaction with v18

claims.statement: Carrier pickup feed is lagging, has failed to receive requests for the 186 orders, or is unable to execute due to dock/staging constraints
claims.corroboration: Observability gap prevents confirmation; Carrier ops on-call found nothing obvious in dock schedule but lacks visibility into order state details
claims.limitation: Cannot confirm without carrier confirmation data or dock capacity audit

claims.statement: East node dock staging capacity is saturated; 186 orders arriving in one cohort exceeds available dock slots, blocking carrier pickup execution
claims.corroboration: Large single-node cohort at single time correlates with v18 change that routes multi-node orders to east first
claims.limitation: No direct evidence; requires real-time dock capacity audit

capability_gaps.capability: Carrier confirmation state for affected orders: did pickup requests reach carrier system, and why were they not executed?
capability_gaps.reason: Observability gap (m8_e09) blocks this; critical to discriminate allocation defect from carrier execution failure

capability_gaps.capability: Split-reservation exception definition and v18 interaction: when is it applied, is it expected on v18, does it intentionally block pickup?
capability_gaps.reason: All 186 orders carry this flag; causality unknown

capability_gaps.capability: East node dock and staging real-time capacity and utilization
capability_gaps.reason: Needed to rule out dock overflow as blocker

next_action.rationale: All 186 stuck orders carry the split-reservation exception flag. Auditing allocation exceptions for east-node orders since 06:00 will determine: (1) is split-reservation a new behavior in v18 or pre-existing, (2) do all split-reservation exceptions hold orders or only these 186, (3) what stock condition triggers the flag. This is the highest-confidence discriminator: if split-reservation is new in v18 and correlates with stock issues only after v18, then H1 is likely; if the flag is pre-existing and all such orders normally clear pickup, then something downstream (H2/H3) is different.
next_action.expected_information_gain: Clarify whether v18 is creating split-reservation flagging incorrectly, and whether split-reservation is intended to block pickup or is a secondary defect
